site.name: codekite
site.summary: codekite-clone Fictional cloud CI/CD service "CodeKite CI" marketing site, focused on the pricing-page usage calculator. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero (YAML code example on the right), 3 feature cards, CTA to pricing | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 3 plan cards (Free / Team / Enterprise) + usage calculator (three slider+number pairs linked two-way: build minutes / concurrency / storage + ARM / macOS / GPU runner checkboxes); right-side sticky monthly total + recommended-plan badge + line-item cost breakdown; below: 16-row plan comparison table; 10-question FAQ accordion; trusted-logo row; 4-column footer | | `docs.html` | Placeholder quickstart page (one YAML example) |

run_plan.goal: Critique and validate the UX of CodeKite’s marketing/pricing experience, with primary focus on the pricing page’s usage calculator, plan recommendation, and cost breakdown; verify adjacent navigation to docs and marketing CTAs across desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: Start at the landing page to validate global navigation, primary CTAs, and overall information scent to the pricing calculator. Then deep-dive the pricing page: exercise all calculator inputs, confirm two-way binding between sliders and numeric fields, verify plan recommendation logic and the sticky monthly total + line-item breakdown, and test the FAQ accordion and plan comparison table. Finish by validating docs entry points and the “Start free trial / Get started / Talk to sales” CTAs, including mobile viewport behavior and potential small tap-target issues.
assumptions: The three calculator slider+number pairs and the runner checkboxes exist on pricing.html and are interactive (two-way linked controls).
pricing.html contains a sticky monthly total area and a recommended-plan badge that update based on calculator inputs.
Docs content is minimal (“Quickstart”) and relies mainly on navigation links rather than complex forms.
Some interactive elements may have accessibility/labeling issues (prescan flagged missing_input_label and small tap targets on both desktop and mobile).
risk_hotspots: pricing.html usage calculator controls: two-way sync between sliders and number inputs for build minutes, concurrency, and storage (plus runner checkboxes for ARM/macOS/GPU).
pricing.html form inputs: prescan indicates missing_input_label for multiple inputs; validate accessible labels, focus order, keyboard behavior, and screen-reader names.
pricing.html sticky monthly total + line-item cost breakdown: risk of not updating correctly or becoming inconsistent with recommended plan badge.
pricing.html small tap targets / tap accuracy on mobile (multiple layout warnings on pricing and nav in prescan).
pricing.html FAQ accordion behavior: ensure only one opens/close correctly, proper toggling states, and scroll/focus handling.

Navigation CTAs (Sign in, Start free trial, Get started, Start trial, Talk to sales): validate expected destinations or graceful non-functional placeholders (prescan shows they exist as links/controls).

phases.title: Landing (index.html) navigation & CTA routing
phases.objective: Validate top navigation and key marketing CTAs lead users to correct destinations and that the page communicates the pricing value proposition clearly.
key_checks: Use top nav links: Product, Pricing, Docs; confirm correct page loads and URL/file changes.
Click “Sign in” (href shown as #): validate whether it opens a modal/dialog, navigates to a sign-in flow, or remains a non-functional placeholder (confirm no dead-end experience).
Click “Start free trial” and “See pricing” and “Read docs”; confirm both lead to expected pages (pricing.html/docs.html).

Scroll to sections with “Overview/Changelog/Status/Security/About/Blog/Careers” anchors (prescan shows # links): verify whether anchors scroll to content or remain placeholders; note if any cause confusing jumps.
exit_criteria: All primary navigation items and CTA buttons (at least: Pricing, Docs, Start free trial, See pricing, Read docs) are confirmed to route to the intended known pages without errors.
Any # placeholder links are characterized (e.g., stay on page with no change vs. open UI), and no unexpected blank state occurs.

phases.title: Pricing calculator: correctness, two-way binding, and live totals
phases.objective: Exercise the usage calculator end-to-end and verify that all dependent UI (recommended plan, sticky monthly total, and line-item breakdown) updates correctly and consistently.
key_checks: Identify all three slider+number pairs (build minutes/month, concurrency, storage) and verify two-way binding: changing slider updates the numeric value; typing a number updates the slider thumb.
Set representative values across the ranges (including low, mid, and near-extreme values) and confirm calculations remain stable and non-janky.
Toggle runner checkboxes (Linux ARM, macOS, GPU runner per prescan labels) and confirm pricing changes and that totals/line items reflect runner-specific surcharges or plan constraints.
Validate plan recommendation badge changes as inputs change (e.g., Free vs Team vs Enterprise) and that the recommendation matches the visual plan tiers.
Validate sticky monthly total updates while scrolling; ensure it remains consistent with the line-item cost breakdown below.
Test edge handling: clearing numeric inputs, entering non-numeric characters, and keyboard increment/decrement behavior (where supported).
exit_criteria: For each of the calculator controls, two-way sync is confirmed at least once, and resulting totals/recommendation/breakdown update coherently across multiple input combinations.
Sticky monthly total and line-item breakdown agree on the final computed cost for at least two different scenarios (one near Free/Team boundary, one that triggers a higher-tier plan).

phases.title: Pricing page content: plan CTAs, comparison table, and FAQ accordion
phases.objective: Validate secondary UX components on pricing.html: plan CTAs, comparison table usability, and FAQ accordion interaction/accessibility.
key_checks: Click plan CTAs: “Get started” / “Start trial” for Free/Team and “Talk to sales” for Enterprise; verify destination behavior (open link, modal, or placeholder) and that user is not stranded.
Test plan cards interaction: focus/hover states (visual affordance) and ensuring no accidental scroll-jumps when selecting.
Exercise the 16-row plan comparison table: confirm headers and row content are readable and not obscured by sticky elements; verify horizontal overflow behavior on smaller widths.
Open and close several FAQ accordion items; confirm correct expanded/collapsed state, no multiple panels incorrectly open (unless intended), and that keyboard focus moves predictably.
exit_criteria: All visible CTA elements on pricing.html are clicked at least once and their resulting behavior is documented as expected or as a known placeholder.
At least 3 FAQ items are successfully expanded/collapsed with correct state persistence and no layout glitches.

phases.title: Adjacent page: Docs (docs.html) and marketing consistency
phases.objective: Ensure the docs entry is discoverable from pricing/landing, and verify the docs page has coherent UX and navigation back to pricing.
key_checks: From docs.html, click top nav Pricing and confirm routing back to pricing.html.
Click “CodeKite” and “Docs” links to ensure consistent header navigation.
Scroll through quickstart content to ensure code blocks are readable and not clipped on desktop; note any copy/format issues (if present).
Click “Start free trial” (if present in header) and confirm it routes properly to pricing.html or intended trial flow.
exit_criteria: Docs page navigation links consistently route to the known pages (index/pricing/docs) with no unexpected dead-ends.
Quickstart content is legible and scannable without obvious visual breakage.

phases.title: Mobile viewport regression: calculator, accordions, and tap targets
phases.objective: Repeat critical flows on mobile viewport to validate tap usability, layout reflow, sticky behavior, and input accessibility.
key_checks: Repeat landing CTA routing: Pricing, Docs, Start free trial; verify header fits and taps are accurate.
On pricing.html, confirm calculator controls remain usable: sliders draggable, numeric inputs focusable, and checkboxes toggle reliably.

Specifically validate small tap targets flagged in prescan (nav items like CodeKite/Product/Pricing/Docs/Sign in): confirm tap success rates and whether any controls are too small for comfortable mobile use.
Validate FAQ accordion tap targets and expanded content visibility; ensure sticky monthly total doesn’t cover content or trap scrolling.
Validate plan CTAs (“Get started”, “Start trial”, “Talk to sales”) remain accessible and readable on mobile.
exit_criteria: All critical interactions from phases 1–3 succeed on mobile at least once (no broken controls, no hidden/covered sticky elements).
Sticky monthly total remains functional/consistent and does not block access to the calculator or FAQ content.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (index.html, pricing.html, docs.html) in both desktop and mobile viewports.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible controls on pricing.html: 3 slider+number pairs, runner checkboxes (ARM/macOS/GPU), plan CTAs, sticky monthly total area (indirect via updates), comparison table readability, and FAQ accordion items.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the calculator update flow plus at least 3 FAQ toggles and the top nav CTA routing on mobile.

notes: Prescan indicates 0 buttons/0 forms at the time of extraction, but pricing.html contains 9 inputs and checkbox-like controls; treat all interactive elements as real controls to validate keyboard and accessibility labeling despite missing_input_label warnings.
Max steps: keep iterations focused on representative value sets and avoid exhaustive combinations; prioritize validating correctness and consistency across dependent UI.

prescan_summary.title: CodeKite CI — Faster builds. Honest bills.
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: CodeKite Product Pricing Docs Sign in Start free trial Faster builds. Honest bills. CodeKite is a CI/CD service that bills you for what you build. No per-seat tax. Bring your .yml and a credit card you'll hopefully never max out. See pricing Read docs version: 2.1 jobs: build: runs-on: linux/x86 steps: - checkout - run: pnpm install - run: pnpm test - cache: path: node_modules key: lock-{{ checksum "pnpm-lock.yaml" }} Parallelism, plain Split a 12-min suite across 16 slots; pay per minute, not per slot. Slots scale to zero when idle. Bill you can read Every invoice breaks down to the job, the runner type, and the minute. Per-team and per-pipeline rollups. Drop-in YAML If you've used Circle or GitHub Actions, you're 90% of the way there. We provide a converter. CodeKite CI Faster builds. Honest bills. PRODUCT Overview Pricing Docs RESOURCES Changelog Status Security COMPANY About Blog Car

prescan_summary.title: CodeKite Docs
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: CodeKite Product Pricing Docs Sign in Quickstart Drop a .codekite.yml at the root of your repo and push. version: 2.1 jobs: test: runs-on: linux/x86 steps: - checkout - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile - run: pnpm test --shard $CK_SHARD/$CK_TOTAL_SHARDS parallel: 8 That's it. Push a commit — your first build runs in under a minute. Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
